topic: Understanding the Determinant: The Geometry of Scaling

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Linear Transformation
lecture_lines: Vectors i and j define a square.
The square deforms into a parallelogram.
animations: Create a 2D grid plane labeled 'Grid' in #FFFFFF.
Show a basis vector i (1,0) in #00FF00.
Show a basis vector j (0,1) in #0000FF.
Illustrate a linear transformation moving i and j.

sections.title: Defining the Determinant
lecture_lines: Determinant is the area scaling factor.
Transformation maps a shape to a region.
It measures the expansion or shrinkage.
animations: Draw a 2x2 square area labeled 'Area' in #FFFF00.
Represent the transformation matrix as a set of vectors.
Show the transformed shape changing size relative to original.

sections.title: The Meaning of Sign and Zero
animations: Show area changing color based on orientation (positive/negative).
Demonstrate mapping to a line (zero determinant) in #FF00FF.
Display zero-area transformation result as a flat line.

sections.title: Calculation Method (The 2x2 Case)
lecture_lines: Use formula det equals ad minus bc.
Connects formula to geometric side lengths.
Example shows unit square becomes rectangle.
animations: Write matrix [a, b; c, d] on screen in #FFFFFF.
Final formula ad-bc appears clearly in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: Determinant is a core diagnostic tool.
Zero means the system is singular.
animations: Display the determinant as a single scaling factor.
Animate shrinking and expanding of a 2D shape.
Summarize determinant use in geometric scaling.
